objectives.requirement: Encrypt sensitive values in the trusted application **before PostgreSQL receives plaintext**, with proof at SQL/driver boundaries and independent connections.

objectives.requirement: Preserve confidentiality and authenticated integrity under declared tenant/field/row/key-generation context, detect swapped or malformed frames and unauthorized release.

objectives.requirement: Enforce application authorization, result lineage and tenant boundaries; handle SQL injection through parameterization, guarded operations and least privilege without falsely claiming that encryption prevents arbitrary application authorization flaws.

objectives.requirement: Detect plaintext bypasses via ORM, bulk DML, direct SQL, COPY, external writers, migrations, sessions, background jobs, triggers, caches, logs, exports, backups and privilege paths.
objectives.note: Requirement text only; stale per-objective evidence/status not promoted

objectives.requirement: Keep payload/search keys isolated, never silently choose fallback keys, bound nonces/usage/leases, test memory/fork/cancellation/rotation and use robust existing cryptography.

objectives.requirement: Reduce equality, frequency and access-pattern leakage with a threat-modelled, independently benchmarked search-profile design; document residual leakage, low-entropy domains, adaptive leakage and query-pattern trade-offs.

objectives.requirement: Independent red-team/security, cryptography, SQL adapter, provider and supply-chain qualification; the seven gates pass only with real evidence.

objectives.requirement: Ordinary SQL correctness: `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`, `!=`, `NOT IN`, `IS DISTINCT FROM`, `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`, nested Boolean expressions, aliases, outer joins, scalar/entity projections, relationships, subqueries.

Each gets native semantics, a viable scheme/profile or an explicit, researched `REJECTED-LOUD` alternative—never silent omission.
